summary: 1939 steel lookout on Mount Grace in Warwick, Massachusetts, built after the 1938 hurricane destroyed its predecessor; staffed during periods of fire danger.

facts.agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control

staffing.status: staffed during periods of fire danger

access.note: Summit and stairs are on public state forest land. The cab was locked when a 2018 hiker visited, and a Pioneer Valley guide says it is open to the public; check before climbing.

visit.trail_note: Trail from the road to the summit is about a mile and a half and gains roughly 1,000 feet

events.note: First tower: 40-ft iron windmill-type tower with a ladder and 6x6 cab
Register says a 68-ft iron tower replaced the windmill in 1920; a 1919 newspaper item gives 71 ft and a state report gives 70 ft steel
Lookout Donald Davidson spotted a fire in New Hampshire and telephoned the alarm
Predecessor tower blown down by the 1938 hurricane (Sept 21, 1938 per the Eastern lookouts site)
Present 68-ft steel tower with 10x10 wooden cab
Registered December 15, 2004 as US 628, MA 39; nominated by Henry Isenberg

corrections.why: 12.2 m is 40 ft, the height of the first (1911) windmill tower. The register gives the present tower as 68 ft, about 20.7 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1911 is the first tower on the summit (a 40-ft windmill); 1939 is the present steel tower built after the 1938 hurricane destroyed its predecessor.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: the 1920 replacement tower is 68 ft iron per the register, 71 ft per a Aug 1919 newspaper item, and 70 ft steel per a 1919 state report. Access is disputed: Pioneer Valley says open to the public; a 2018 hiker found the top locked; the 2016 register visit reports say staffed only in fire-danger periods. Access level is set to restricted as a judgment call and should be checked with DCR. Agency: the register says Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control while Pioneer Valley calls the forest a DCR property; the register wording is kept. Elevation 488.3 m (1,602 ft) is the register's figure; Wikipedia gives 1,617 ft and Pioneer Valley gives DCR's 1,621 ft for the summit, so the record was not changed. A Pioneer Valley photo credit (Aug 2013, CC BY-SA 3.0) is noted but no image URL was found, so no photo entry. Two FFLA Massachusetts Facebook posts (1922 and 1920s photos) appeared in search results only and were not read.
